suites.observable_behavior: Offline editable installation, Django 5.2 compatibility of the exercised code paths, django-taggit declared as an extra, every public name importable from its exact module path, and subclass safety of fields and managers.
suites.case_design: Pinned offline image, network none, read-only checker mount, PIP_NO_INDEX=1. Copy the candidate into a fresh writable directory and run its real setup.sh in a fresh virtual environment that sees the preinstalled system packages; record argv and exit code. From a new empty directory, import modelcluster and assert __file__ resolves into the copied tree; read importlib.metadata for Requires-Dist/Provides-Extra. A checker-owned settings module (in-memory SQLite, USE_TZ=True, INSTALLED_APPS: contenttypes, auth, taggit, the checker test app, plus modelcluster only if the case variant requires it) drives one subprocess per case: import probes, a to_json call on an aware datetime, and checker subclasses of ParentalKey, ParentalManyToManyField and type(band.members) carrying generic private attribute names.

suites.observable_behavior: ParentalKey field type and default on_delete, the deferring child manager's in-memory assignment/all/add/remove/clear/create/set/count/read API, commit() row synchronisation and IntegrityError, Meta.ordering of in-memory children, and the modelcluster.E001/E002 and fields.E300 system checks.
suites.case_design: After the real setup.sh install, each case runs in its own subprocess with the checker-owned settings module and checker-authored Band/BandMember/PlainModel test models whose tables are created with the schema editor in an in-memory SQLite database. Row counts are read with plain ORM queries on the child table; DB state before and after save/commit is compared. System-check cases build isolated models in a throwaway app registry (isolate_apps) and call field.check()/model.check(), comparing error ids and exact msg strings.

suites.observable_behavior: ParentalManyToManyField manager semantics held in memory, assignment equivalent to set(), the manager's model attribute, empty fresh reads, ValueError for unsaved targets, target Meta.ordering, the reverse accessor reflecting saved parents only, value_from_object returning the in-memory set, and save(update_fields) committing a named m2m.
suites.case_design: Checker-authored Article(ClusterableModel) with authors = ParentalManyToManyField(Author, related_name='articles_by_author') and an Author model with Meta.ordering, tables created in in-memory SQLite. Through-table rows are counted directly via Article.authors.through.objects before and after each save; reverse-accessor results are read from freshly fetched Author instances. One subprocess per case after the real setup.sh install.

suites.observable_behavior: FakeQuerySet construction and filter/exclude over in-memory instances: every listed lookup type, value coercion, None/empty handling, Python-membership in, lookup-named fields, forward and parent relation traversal with None intermediates, instance and multi-table-inheritance matching, Q combinations, ManyToManyTraversalError, and date/time transforms and their conventions.
suites.case_design: Checker-authored models (Log, Album with DateField, a DateTimeField model, a TimeField model, a model with a field named range, Chef/Restaurant/Diner with nullable FKs and a one-to-one, Place/Restaurant multi-table inheritance) built as unsaved or saved instances and wrapped with FakeQuerySet(model, list) or reached through band.members. Expected values are computed independently in the checker from the instance attributes. The parity case saves the cluster and runs the identical lookup battery against the real SQLite queryset, comparing results row by row. One subprocess per case after the real setup.sh install.

suites.observable_behavior: get() with DoesNotExist/MultipleObjectsReturned and shaped results, count/exists/first/last, order_by including relations, None-first and '?', values/values_list including flat and its TypeError, distinct, none(), all() and chaining, the sequence protocol, accepted select_related/only/defer, and query-reducing prefetch_related.
suites.case_design: In-memory FakeQuerySets over checker-authored models in in-memory SQLite. Exception types are asserted against model.DoesNotExist and model.MultipleObjectsReturned. Prefetch cases save several parents with children and parental m2m targets, then count queries with django.test.utils.CaptureQueriesContext for two parent counts, comparing prefetched and non-prefetched loops; '?' ordering is checked only as a permutation. One subprocess per case after the real setup.sh install.

suites.observable_behavior: ClusterableModel abstractness and keyword constructor, save() committing every child relation and parental m2m, update_fields partitioning, get_all_child_relations/get_all_child_m2m_relations introspection including inheritance, and copy_cluster/copy_child_relation/copy_all_child_relations results, maps, overwrite/append and commit semantics.
suites.case_design: Checker-authored Band (members, albums, genres parental m2m, fans plain m2m), clusterable Album with Song children, Place/Restaurant multi-table inheritance with Review and MenuItem children and a plain Visit FK, all in in-memory SQLite. Cases compare DB rows before and after save calls, inspect relation objects returned by the helpers, and inspect copies and returned maps by identity and pk. One subprocess per case after the real setup.sh install.

suites.observable_behavior: serializable_data() structure (pk, full concrete field set including multi-table-inherited fields, field-name keys, serialize=False omission, recursive children, m2m pks), to_json(), from_json/from_serializable_data rebuild including pk propagation up the inheritance chain, check_fks/strict_fks resolution, Meta.ordering re-sort, UTC datetime handling and FileField round-trips.
suites.case_design: Checker-owned settings with USE_TZ=True and TIME_ZONE='Asia/Seoul', MEDIA_ROOT in a per-case temporary directory, in-memory SQLite. Expected dicts are built in the checker from instance attributes; JSON is compared after json.loads. Dangling-FK cases serialize first, delete the referenced rows with QuerySet.delete(), then deserialize. Datetime cases parse the emitted ISO strings and compare instants. One subprocess per case after the real setup.sh install.

suites.observable_behavior: transientmodelformset_factory and childformset_factory behaviour (FK exclusion, existing plus extra forms, staged versus committed save, validate_max/validate_min codes, sort_order_field ORDER, nested formsets, default 'form' prefix) and ClusterForm Meta options, formsets attributes, composite validation, uniqueness, rendering/media/multipart, inherit_kwargs, save(commit) with save_m2m, and clusterform_factory.
suites.case_design: Checker-authored forms and models (Band with members/albums, clusterable Album with songs, a child with sort_order_field, children with unique_together and UniqueConstraint, Article with parental m2m, ClusterTaggableManager tags and a plain m2m) in in-memory SQLite. Bound data dicts are written by the checker with explicit management-form keys. Assertions read is_valid(), non_form_errors().as_data() codes, widget classes, form.media JS lists, isinstance(as_p(), SafeString), formsets dict keys and DB rows before and after each save step. One subprocess per case after the real setup.sh install.

suites.observable_behavior: ClusterTaggableManager subclassing taggit's TaggableManager with a ParentalKey through model, in-memory add/remove/clear/set/count/all on unsaved and saved owners, ValueError for non-string non-Tag values, prefetch_related('tags'), and tag fields (cluster-aware and plain TaggableManager) through ClusterForm.
suites.case_design: Settings include the preinstalled taggit app; checker-authored TaggedPlace(TaggedItemBase) with a ParentalKey content_object and Place(ClusterableModel) with ClusterTaggableManager, plus a second ClusterableModel with a plain TaggableManager, all in in-memory SQLite. Tagged-item rows are counted directly; prefetch cases use CaptureQueriesContext over two owner counts. One subprocess per case after the real setup.sh install.

normal_control.description: A minimal reference package written only from instruction.md: a setup.sh and pyproject.toml performing an offline editable install with django-taggit under an extra; modelcluster.models (abstract ClusterableModel with keyword constructor, save/update_fields partitioning, introspection helpers, serializable_data/to_json/from_serializable_data/from_json with check_fks/strict_fks and UTC datetimes, copy_cluster/copy_child_relation/copy_all_child_relations); modelcluster.fields (ParentalKey with E001/E002 checks and the deferring child manager, ParentalManyToManyField with its in-memory manager and value_from_object); modelcluster.queryset.FakeQuerySet covering every listed lookup, transform and retrieval method; modelcluster.utils.ManyToManyTraversalError; modelcluster.forms (transientmodelformset_factory, childformset_factory, ClusterForm, clusterform_factory); and modelcluster.contrib.taggit.ClusterTaggableManager. Every planned case must pass against it in the pinned image. It validates that the checker cases are satisfiable and discriminating; it never certifies a candidate, and its passing results say nothing about hidden tests.

defective_controls.mutation: setup.sh runs pip install without --no-index and adds django-taggit as an install target, so it fails with the network disabled.
Datetime serialization in modelcluster.models uses django.utils.timezone.utc instead of datetime.timezone.utc.
pyproject.toml lists django-taggit as an unconditional dependency and declares no extra.
ManyToManyTraversalError is defined in modelcluster.queryset and modelcluster/utils.py does not exist.
The deferring manager keeps its in-memory list in self._items and resolves it through the instance, so a checker subclass defining _items breaks assignment and all().
ClusterableModel.save() saves the parent row but never commits child relations.
ParentalKey defaults on_delete to models.DO_NOTHING when omitted.
Assigning parent.members = [...] appends to the in-memory set instead of replacing it.
all() on an unsaved, untouched parent delegates to the database related manager, which raises ValueError for an unsaved instance.
add() appends every object without replacing an equal one already present.
create(**kwargs) calls child.save() before appending it.
The manager's count() returns the database row count instead of the in-memory set size.
commit() saves current members but never deletes database rows missing from the in-memory set.
commit() on a parent without a pk returns without raising.
The in-memory child set keeps insertion order and ignores the child's Meta.ordering.
The E001 message omits its trailing period.
ParentalKey.check() does not emit modelcluster.E002 for related_name='+'.
E001 is emitted when the target is an unresolved model name string.
The parental m2m manager writes through rows immediately on add/remove/set when the parent has a pk, and clear() deletes through rows at once.
Assigning parent.authors = [...] on an unsaved parent raises ValueError.
The parental m2m manager does not expose a model attribute.
add() accepts related objects without a pk.
The in-memory related set keeps insertion order and ignores the target model's Meta.ordering.
The field forces related_name='+', so no reverse accessor is created on the target model.
value_from_object falls back to ManyToManyField's implementation, returning empty for unsaved instances.
save(update_fields=[...]) ignores parental m2m names instead of committing them.
FakeQuerySet stores its results sorted by pk instead of in the given list order.
exclude() returns the same rows as filter().
iexact, icontains, istartswith, iendswith and iregex compare case-sensitively.
range excludes its upper bound.
Lookup values are compared raw without conversion to the field's Python type, so id='2' does not match pk 2.
in never matches a None field value even when None is in the list.
The last __-free segment is parsed as a lookup when it names a lookup type, so a field named range is treated as the range lookup.
Relation traversal dereferences a None intermediate and raises AttributeError.
Instance comparison uses pk only, so two distinct unsaved instances (pk None) match.
Q objects combined with XOR are evaluated as OR.
Traversing a many-to-many relation in a lookup returns no rows instead of raising ManyToManyTraversalError.
values() and values_list() reject transform paths such as release_date__year.
week_day is computed with isoweekday() (Monday = 1).
Deriving a component from a None datetime raises AttributeError instead of yielding None.
get() returns the first match when several rows match instead of raising MultipleObjectsReturned.
order_by() places rows with a None sort value last.
values('band') yields the related instance instead of its pk.
values_list(..., flat=True) with two fields returns tuples instead of raising TypeError.
distinct() without arguments compares all fields including the pk, so no rows are dropped.
filter() on a none() queryset re-reads the original results.
FakeQuerySet.prefetch_related returns self without calling prefetch_related_objects, and child relation descriptors expose no prefetch support.
ClusterableModel.__init__ discards child-relation and parental-m2m keyword arguments.
save() commits child relations but not parental m2m fields.
save(update_fields=...) passes relation names through to Django's save, which raises ValueError.
get_all_child_relations inspects only relations declared against the model itself, omitting ancestors.
get_all_child_m2m_relations returns every ManyToManyField, including plain ones.
copy_cluster keeps the original primary keys on copied children.
copy_child_relation keeps the target's existing children when append is False.
The (child_relation, None) map entry holds the last copied object instead of a list.
copy_all_child_relations copies every relation regardless of exclude.
serializable_data serializes children's concrete fields only, without recursing into clusterable children's relations.
serializable_data iterates _meta.local_fields, omitting fields inherited from a multi-table parent.
Foreign keys are serialized under their attname (band_id).
from_serializable_data sets pk and the *_ptr_id links but not the root model's own primary-key attribute.
A dangling CASCADE FK on the base object is nullified even when strict_fks is True.
A child with a dangling CASCADE FK is kept with that FK set to None instead of being dropped.
Deserialized children keep the order of the serialized list.
Naive datetimes are labelled UTC without interpreting them in the current time zone.
FileFields are skipped by serializable_data.
The transient formset's save(commit=False) saves each instance.
childformset_factory leaves the ParentalKey as a required form field.
The child formset's save(commit=False) writes added and edited children to the database.
max_num and min_num are validated even when validate_max/validate_min are False.
Submitted ORDER values are not copied to the child's sort_order_field.
childformset_factory ignores formsets=[...] when form is a ClusterForm.
childformset_factory formsets default their prefix to the relation accessor name.
A ClusterForm with neither formsets nor exclude_formsets builds formsets for every child relation.
Meta.exclude_formsets is ignored.
A child-relation key in Meta.widgets is not passed to that formset.
ClusterForm considers only child relations declared on the model itself.
ClusterForm child formsets default to one extra form.
Child forms marked for deletion are still validated.
unique_together and UniqueConstraint are not checked across submitted child forms.
as_p() renders only the parent form.
Every ClusterForm constructor kwarg is forwarded to child forms regardless of inherit_kwargs.
ClusterForm.save(commit=False) defers parental m2m and tag fields to save_m2m().
modelcluster.forms does not define clusterform_factory.
ClusterTaggableManager is TaggableManager with no in-memory relation, so tag changes on unsaved instances fail and saved ones write immediately.
tags.remove() leaves the in-memory set unchanged.
tags.add(1) coerces the integer to the tag name '1'.
The tags manager does not support prefetching, so prefetch_related('tags') raises.
ClusterForm drops submitted tag strings for ClusterTaggableManager fields.
